title: Kingston: art, music and the making of a capital
duration: One full day; split into two for long museum visits
question: Who gets to represent Jamaica, and what changes when you hear the city from its own communities?
walk: Walk only short waterfront stretches and venue grounds. Downtown, Trench Town and Devon House are separate transfers.
drive: Book a driver for waterfront → Trench Town → Devon House, with pickups agreed at each venue. Leave afternoon room for traffic.
public: Arrive in Kingston by a bookable Knutsford Express service, then transfer from the actual terminal. JUTC can help with city legs: use its current route guide and confirm the stop and return; no single bus is claimed to join all three venues.
call: Make the Culture Yard booking the anchor. A local guide and a thoughtful museum visit teach more than collecting murals from a moving car.
access: Ask each museum about entrance steps, toilets and seated tour options. Vehicle transfers reduce walking; they do not establish step-free interiors.
cost: Budget for gallery/tour admission, a meal and separate transfers; use current operator quotes.

stops.name: National Gallery of Jamaica
stops.activity: Choose a few works rather than rushing every room. Compare how Jamaican artists depict work, race, religion and the landscape. The published visitor page excludes Mondays and public holidays.
stops.leg: Start at the booked gallery; check its current exhibition and admission.

stops.name: Kingston waterfront
stops.activity: Take a short daylight pause near the gallery. Read the harbour as an entrance for trade and migration; compare the view with the guide’s railway and city history.
stops.leg: Short local walk if the actual street conditions suit you; otherwise use your pickup.

stops.name: Trench Town Culture Yard
stops.activity: Take an arranged guided visit. Ask about housing, shared yards and the musicians’ community, then connect the place with ska, rocksteady and reggae in the listening room.
stops.leg: Vehicle or a confirmed local public-transport connection; agree the guide’s meeting point.

stops.name: Devon House
stops.activity: Book the mansion tour if architecture is your interest; otherwise use the grounds and a meal pause. Compare this elite domestic setting with the housing story you heard in Trench Town.
stops.leg: Separate vehicle transfer; allow this to be the final substantial stop.

reading.label: Hear the history behind Jamaican music

title: Blue Mountains: water, coffee and a cooler landscape
duration: One mountain day; no summit climb included
question: How do elevation, water and agricultural work shape the mountain landscape?
walk: Walk at the booked coffee visit and on an appropriate Holywell trail. Do not walk the entire Gordon Town–Irish Town–Holywell road corridor.
drive: Use a mountain-experienced driver for Kingston → Gordon Town → Irish Town → Holywell and return. Ask about the road approach, rain and visibility before departure.
public: A coach can bring you to Kingston; it does not take this excursion into Holywell. Ask locally about buses or route taxis to Gordon Town, then arrange a confirmed onward vehicle and return. A driver is the simpler complete-day option.
call: Choose Holywell and one booked coffee encounter. A peak hike is another trip, requiring different timing and arrangements.
access: Ask park management to identify the exact trail gradient, surface and toilets. A cafe view can replace a walk, but verify its approach and seating.
cost: Allow for park entry, a booked coffee experience, food and a full-day vehicle quote.

stops.name: Gordon Town
stops.activity: Pause with your driver at a suitable public place. Look at the river valley and town connections; discuss water, hillside settlement and everyday travel rather than treating the town as scenery.
stops.leg: First mountain-road leg; stop only where the driver identifies legal, suitable parking.

stops.name: Irish Town: a coffee and meal pause
stops.activity: Use a confirmed cafe stop for coffee and a valley view. If you want cultivation and processing explained, arrange a named farm tour separately; buying a cup is not a farm visit.
stops.leg: Continue uphill by vehicle; confirm the cafe’s opening and whether a tour is included.

stops.name: Holywell Recreation Area
stops.activity: Choose a park-managed walk suited to your group. Observe forest cover, mist and water catchment; ask the guide how conservation connects to communities below.
stops.leg: Vehicle to the confirmed park entrance, then the selected trail on foot.

stops.name: Return through the mountain corridor
stops.activity: Leave time for daylight driving and a slower return after rain. Compare the cooler forest with the lower city landscape and record what you actually observed.
stops.leg: Return in the arranged vehicle; no roadside viewpoint is promised as an open attraction.

title: St. Ann: Taíno landscapes, enslavement and Garvey
duration: One weekday; allow a full day from Ocho Rios
base: Ocho Rios, St. Ann’s Bay or western St. Ann
question: What becomes visible when Seville’s estate story is read alongside African Jamaican lives and a working town?
walk: Walk the confirmed Seville visitor route and a short St. Ann’s Bay town branch. Transfer between the estate, town and Drax Hall.
drive: From Ocho Rios travel west to Seville, back to St. Ann’s Bay, then toward Drax Hall for the meal and return. Choose this branch instead of adding Nine Mile.
public: Book a coach to the passenger terminal serving your St. Ann base; confirm whether your ticket uses Drax Hall or another pickup. Arrange local licensed taxis for Seville and the town. Local coastal buses require stop and return confirmation.
call: Book Seville first. On a weekend or public holiday, choose the town and reading instead, or move the estate visit to a suitable weekday.
access: Ask Seville about the actual museum approach and grounds surfaces. Town pavements and crossings need their own assessment.
cost: Seville admission/tour, local transport and a meal; confirm resident/non-resident terms directly.

stops.name: Seville Heritage Park
stops.activity: Take the booked guided visit. Ask which objects relate to Taíno life, European settlement and African labour, and which people remain unnamed in the estate record.
stops.leg: Start with the confirmed weekday booking; JNHT publishes weekday hours and holiday closure.

stops.name: St. Ann’s Bay town and Garvey connection
stops.activity: Visit public town spaces and use the 32 Market Street heritage account to understand Garvey’s connection. Do not assume entry to a birthplace or private building.
stops.leg: Short drive from Seville, then a locally planned town walk.

stops.name: St. Ann’s Bay shore and working landscape
stops.activity: Observe the harbour from a permitted public position. Compare work, buildings and coast with historical material; request permission before photographing people at work.
stops.leg: Local branch chosen with your guide; no entry to an active wharf is implied.

stops.name: Drax Hall: food and a pause
stops.activity: Have a jerk meal and discuss preparation with the cook if the service allows. Leave the final block for an unhurried return rather than another distant attraction.
stops.leg: Vehicle toward Drax Hall; arrange the pickup before sitting down.

reading.label: Ocho Rios and St. Ann in history

title: St. Mary: working towns, ports and public memory
duration: One coastal day from a St. Mary base
question: What does a working coastline reveal that a celebrity-house itinerary leaves out?
walk: Use separate short walks in Oracabessa and Port Maria. The coast between them is a vehicle journey.
drive: Follow Oracabessa → Port Maria; add Firefly only with confirmed access and enough time for its separate uphill approach.
public: Check a bookable coach journey to Port Maria or your actual nearest passenger stop; arrange the terminal transfer. Licensed coastal route taxis may serve town legs after local confirmation. Firefly needs its own arranged return.
call: Two towns and one confirmed house visit are enough. Castleton and inland Highgate belong to another day.
access: Ask about pavement, shade, toilets and the house’s steps. Use a vehicle-assisted exterior town route if a full walk is unsuitable.
cost: Town viewing, a meal, local transfers and Firefly admission if booked; agree driver waiting time.

stops.name: Oracabessa town
stops.activity: Walk a short public main-street branch and compare its present buildings with the guide’s historical town photograph. Ask how harbour work and agriculture shaped the settlement.
stops.leg: Begin locally; agree the end of the walk and vehicle meeting point.

stops.name: Port Maria courthouse and town
stops.activity: Use the courthouse heritage account to connect architecture, public administration and remembrance. View from a permitted public position; institutional business takes priority.
stops.leg: Coastal transfer, then a short daylight town walk.

stops.name: Port Maria harbour and meal
stops.activity: Take a meal break and observe the bay from a public place. Listen to contemporary town life; avoid treating residents as an exhibit.
stops.leg: Remain in the town branch; the guide/driver identifies a suitable stop.

stops.name: Firefly, if your booking is confirmed
stops.activity: Compare a celebrated writer’s house and view with the working towns below. If access is unavailable, extend the Port Maria visit and reading instead.
stops.leg: Separate vehicle leg and return; do not rely on finding a return ride at the house.

reading.label: Port Maria: the town behind the view

title: Portland: harbour, town houses and the jerk coast
duration: Two relaxed days; one town day and one coastal day
question: How do harbour trade, domestic architecture, food and coastal life connect?
walk: Walk a modest Port Antonio/Titchfield branch with a local guide. Boston and Frenchman’s Cove require separate road transfers.
drive: Day 1 stays in Port Antonio. Day 2 follows Port Antonio → Frenchman’s Cove → Boston Bay and returns; choose Reach Falls on another day.
public: Knutsford Express has a Port Antonio booking option; confirm the passenger arrival and transfer into town. On the coastal day, use a licensed driver or locally confirmed buses/route taxis with a planned return; no door-to-door coach excursion is implied.
call: Give the harbour town a real day. Reach Falls, rafting and a Maroon community visit each deserve separate arrangements.
access: Titchfield streets can be sloped and uneven. Ask the cove operator about its actual entrance, toilets and beach approach; sand is a separate barrier.
cost: Local guiding/transfers, food, and cove or beach charges from the chosen operator.

stops.name: Port Antonio harbour and town
stops.activity: Begin with a guide in the working town. Read the harbour in relation to trade and travel; compare what the guide documents with what you can see today.
stops.leg: Transfer from the actual terminal; short town walk from an agreed meeting point.

stops.name: Titchfield Peninsula
stops.activity: Look at house forms, verandas and streets from public space. Use the historic-district account and the guide’s Titchfield essay; enter a private house only by invitation.
stops.leg: Local town branch on foot or with vehicle assistance.

stops.name: Frenchman’s Cove
stops.activity: Use a booked beach visit to observe the meeting of stream and sea. Swimming is optional and depends on actual conditions; a forecast does not inspect the water.
stops.leg: Coastal vehicle journey from Port Antonio; confirm the entrance and pickup.

stops.name: Boston Bay and jerk cooks
stops.activity: Take your time over a meal. Ask about fuel, seasoning and cooking when the cook can talk; compare multiple preparations without proclaiming a single stall the origin of all jerk.
stops.leg: Continue east by arranged vehicle; make Boston Beach an optional extension, then return.

reading.label: Moore Town: arrange a separate community visit

title: Montego Bay and Falmouth: ports, resistance and preservation
duration: Two days; one town per day
question: How do public memorials and preserved buildings tell different stories about the same economy?
walk: Take separate guided town walks around Sam Sharpe Square and central Falmouth. Do not walk the inter-town coastal road.
drive: Day 1 is downtown Montego Bay. Day 2 transfers to Falmouth, stays in its town branch and returns or uses a Falmouth overnight.
public: Check coach booking options for Montego Bay and Falmouth, including the exact passenger terminals. A terminal transfer is separate from the heritage walk. Locally confirmed buses can connect towns; leave room for waiting and a return.
call: Read the labour and resistance history before admiring Georgian facades. Confirm today’s access and recovery conditions in Falmouth with the named guide.
access: Town paving, crossings and old interiors vary. Request a seated museum option and short exterior walking route; do not infer access from heritage designation.
cost: Museum admission, named guiding, food and inter-town travel; interior tours may be separately charged.

stops.name: Sam Sharpe Square and Cultural Centre
stops.activity: Use the museum/gallery and square together. Ask how the town commemorates resistance and how the exhibits explain the plantation economy.
stops.leg: Start in downtown Montego Bay at the confirmed museum or guide meeting point.

stops.name: Harmony Beach Park
stops.activity: Take a public-space pause. Compare who uses a town park with the private resort coast, and leave time for a downtown meal.
stops.leg: Separate short local transfer or a guide-selected walk suited to street conditions.

stops.name: Falmouth streets and courthouse setting
stops.activity: Take a guided exterior walk through the historic district. Compare street layout, civic buildings and domestic architecture; verify any requested interior access.
stops.leg: Inter-town vehicle/coach journey, then a locally confirmed town route.

stops.name: Falmouth wharf landscape
stops.activity: From permitted public space, discuss port trade and the labour behind architectural wealth. Compare historic material with current repairs without entering fenced, damaged or active port areas.
stops.leg: Stay within the guide’s safe town branch; return to the booked pickup.

reading.label: Melissa and Falmouth: documented damage and recovery

title: Negril and Hanover: beach life and a working parish town
duration: Two days; Negril first, Lucea on a separate day
question: What changes when you leave the beach strip and give a western parish town equal attention?
walk: Walk a chosen beach segment and a short Lucea town branch. Beach, Negril town and Lucea are separate journeys.
drive: Day 1 links a permitted Negril beach entrance with a town meal. Day 2 goes to Lucea and a prearranged Fort Charlotte branch; return by vehicle.
public: Book coach travel to Negril and confirm the terminal-to-lodging transfer. For Lucea, confirm the local licensed coastal service and return before setting out; a Negril coach ticket is not a Fort Charlotte tour.
call: Give Lucea its own day. A beach sunset and a fort visit do not need to compete against a late return.
access: Ask the beach host about the actual path and toilets. Lucea’s fort approach and town surfaces need separate confirmation; offer a town-only alternative.
cost: Beach-host amenities if used, town meals, local guiding and transport. Confirm any fort visit terms.

stops.name: A chosen Negril beach segment
stops.activity: Enter through an agreed park or business access. Walk a manageable segment, observe tourism and coastal work, and choose a dry visit or swim according to conditions.
stops.leg: Local transfer to the specific beach entrance, not a generic pin for Seven Mile Beach.

stops.name: Negril town and a Jamaican meal
stops.activity: Move into town for a meal rather than assuming the resort strip represents the whole area. Confirm the restaurant’s opening and ask what is being cooked that day.
stops.leg: Vehicle/local taxi between the beach and town; arrange the return.

stops.name: Lucea town and harbour
stops.activity: With a local guide, look at the civic centre and harbour from public places. Read the Lucea essay and compare its town story with the beach economy.
stops.leg: Separate coastal journey to Lucea; begin at an agreed town meeting point.

stops.name: Fort Charlotte, with arranged access
stops.activity: Ask the guide to connect fortification and harbour geography. If site access is unavailable, remain in Lucea’s public town branch; do not improvise entry.
stops.leg: Confirm the approach and return vehicle before leaving the town centre.

title: St. Thomas: justice, a village and the waters of Bath
duration: Two days; Morant Bay/Stony Gut, then Bath
base: Morant Bay or a southeastern stay
question: How does the story of 1865 change when you move from the courthouse to the community, then to a different landscape of healing and work?
walk: Use short guided walks at public town/village places and the garden when access is confirmed. The town, village and Bath are vehicle legs.
drive: Day 1 follows Morant Bay → an arranged Stony Gut visit and returns. Day 2 follows Morant Bay → Bath garden → the official fountain facility and returns.
public: Confirm licensed buses or route taxis serving Morant Bay from your base and the exact onward services locally. No direct Knutsford Express service to these stops is asserted. A local driver with an agreed return is the simplest multi-stop arrangement.
call: Make the village visit an invitation-based encounter. Do not turn a church, community or healing tradition into an unannounced performance.
access: Ask about slopes, uneven ground, toilets and bathing-facility access. The mineral-water stop can be a discussion visit without bathing.
cost: Guiding, two local vehicle days or confirmed public legs, meals and any official bathing service; agree charges before using services.

stops.name: Morant Bay courthouse and fort landscape
stops.activity: Read the guide’s 1865 history alongside the public memorial landscape. Separate surviving fabric, later restoration and present remembrance.
stops.leg: Meet the local guide at a confirmed accessible public position; interior entry is separate.

stops.name: Stony Gut, by arrangement
stops.activity: Visit with a community contact or guide who has confirmed permission. Discuss congregation, neighbours and collective action; ask before taking portraits or entering a churchyard.
stops.leg: Vehicle to the confirmed meeting point and return; no unscheduled community programme is promised.

stops.name: Bath Botanic Garden
stops.activity: Confirm access, then examine the garden as an institution and a landscape. Follow the Bath garden essay and identify plants only when supported by a label or informed guide.
stops.leg: Separate Bath day; driver confirms the current road and entrance.
stops.mapQuery: Bath Botanic Garden St Thomas Jamaica

stops.name: Bath Fountain official facility
stops.activity: Use the official agency contact to arrange the actual service. If bathing is not wanted or suitable, learn about the place without using the water; do not confuse the facility with unsolicited roadside offers.
stops.leg: Short local transfer as agreed; confirm price, service and return before arrival.

title: South Coast: river town, pepper shrimp and fish with bammy
duration: Two days; avoid making the whole south coast one circuit
question: How do a river port, roadside food and fishing communities tell the story of this coast?
walk: Take a short Black River town walk and brief vendor stops. Town, river operator and food districts require arranged transfers.
drive: Day 1 pairs Black River town with a named river operator. Day 2 travels to Middle Quarters and Border/Scott’s Cove, then returns to your base. Ask the driver for the practical order from your accommodation.
public: Ask Knutsford Express which bookable passenger stop serves your base; use a confirmed local transfer from that stop. Do not assume a direct coach to Black River, Treasure Beach or either vendor district. Licensed local buses/route taxis need current route and return confirmation.
call: Choose two food stops on a separate day and leave time to talk. YS Falls and Treasure Beach can replace a day; they are not compulsory additions.
access: Ask the boat operator about boarding, seating, lifejackets and toilets. Roadside stalls vary in surfaces and seating; arrange a vehicle-assisted stop.
cost: Named river tour, transport, two food purchases and meals. Vendors and operators set their own current prices.

stops.name: Black River town
stops.activity: Take a guide-selected public High Street branch. Compare river trade and town houses with the Black River essay; historic designation does not open private interiors.
stops.leg: Start in town; agree a short walk and a vehicle-assisted alternative.

stops.name: Black River with a named river operator
stops.activity: Choose a booked excursion. Observe wetland habitat with the guide, follow boat instructions and keep distance from wildlife; confirm water/weather conditions with the operator.
stops.leg: Transfer to the actual operator’s dock; return pickup and boarding arrangements are separate.

stops.name: Middle Quarters pepper shrimp
stops.activity: Buy from an operating vendor and ask about preparation when the work allows. Make the food itself the encounter; do not assume a universal recipe or a scheduled demonstration.
stops.leg: Separate road journey on the food day; stop where the driver can park suitably.

stops.name: Border / Scott’s Cove: fish and bammy
stops.activity: Choose a stall actually cooking that day. Ask what fish is available and how the bammy is prepared, then eat without rushing. This stop sits at the St. Elizabeth–Westmoreland border.
stops.leg: Arrange the onward trip and return; Border is not a Negril beach stop.

reading.label: Black River and its port economy
Accompong: a separate arranged community day

title: Central Jamaica: civic power, inland towns and a southern meal
duration: Three days or three independent outings
base: Use a suitable local base for each day
question: What do St. Catherine, Manchester and Clarendon reveal when Jamaica is read from its inland towns?
walk: Use short guided walks in Spanish Town and Mandeville. Clarendon’s meal branch is a vehicle outing; do not walk between parishes.
drive: Day 1: Spanish Town civic centre. Day 2: Mandeville square and parish-church surroundings. Day 3: a May Pen town pause followed by a confirmed Alligator Pond/Little Ochie meal. The final branch crosses into the southern coastal landscape; allow a separate day.
public: Check bookable Knutsford Express journeys serving Spanish Town/Angels, Mandeville or May Pen and confirm the actual passenger stop. Terminal-to-town transfers are separate. JUTC can support the metropolitan Spanish Town leg; local licensed transport/driver arrangements are needed for the southern meal branch.
call: Treat these as three local days, not a speed run. If you have only one day, choose the town nearest your base and read the other two.
access: Working civic spaces, church grounds, uneven paving and the coastal restaurant have different access conditions. Ask for a short exterior town route and confirm restaurant approach and toilets.
cost: Town guiding, intercity journeys, local transfers and the seafood meal. Choose the fish and agree its price before it is prepared.

stops.name: Spanish Town and Emancipation Square
stops.activity: Take a confirmed guided civic-centre route. Read architecture alongside colonial administration and emancipation; distinguish public exterior viewing from a museum or building booking.
stops.leg: Travel to the actual town meeting point; Angels is not the square.

stops.name: Mandeville square and courthouse
stops.activity: Use a daylight town walk to compare the civic centre with Manchester’s later parish history. Court business comes first; view from permitted public space.
stops.leg: Separate Manchester day and terminal transfer; do not append this to Spanish Town as a quick detour.

stops.name: Mandeville parish-church surroundings
stops.activity: Use the parish essay to connect religious institutions with town formation. Ask permission for any interior/grounds visit and avoid interrupting services.
stops.leg: Short local branch chosen by the guide; adapt for pavements and traffic.

stops.name: May Pen pause, then Alligator Pond / Little Ochie
stops.activity: Begin with a modest public town pause in May Pen, then make a separately confirmed coastal seafood outing. At the restaurant ask about the catch, cooking method and price before ordering.
stops.leg: A separate Clarendon-to-coast vehicle day. Confirm the road, restaurant service and return; this is not a coach drop-off at the restaurant.

reading.label: Spanish Town: civic power and everyday life
